name: tool.guide
title: Agent guide
summary: The guide for an AI agent that works with ReqSeq: the steps from need to verification degree with the command of each step, the rules, and the types, statuses and evidence locations of this workspace; with `skill`, the skill file instead, and with `instructions`, the MCP server instructions.
details: The text is the same in every access for the same input. `names` chooses whether commands appear as command-line calls or as MCP tool names; the calls for a pipeline are always command-line calls. Without a workspace, or with a metamodel that cannot be read, the guide leaves out the facts of the metamodel and says why; without a workspace it names the call that creates one. With `skill`, the output is the skill file `managing-requirements` in the format of Agent Skills: the workflows as numbered steps, each command as MCP tool and command-line call, no name of the metamodel, and the version of ReqSeq and a checksum in its frontmatter. With `write`, it is written at two places, in this order, each on its own: `.claude/skills/managing-requirements/SKILL.md`, where Claude Code looks, and `.agents/skills/managing-requirements/SKILL.md`, where other clients look, both in the root of the Git repository of the workspace folder, or in the workspace folder without Git. At each place, a file that ReqSeq did not write, or that was changed since, is replaced only with `replace`, which holds for every place. Through the API and the MCP server, a place outside the repositories of the workspace is refused with the command-line call that writes the file. A folder `.agents/skills` linked to `.claude/skills` inside the repository finds the file the first place wrote, so the second place is `unchanged`; a link at `SKILL.md` itself is refused. When a place is not written, the other places are written all the same and the call fails: the error has the code of the first place not written, names each place with its result, and lists them in `details.places`. With `instructions`, the output is what the MCP server sends as its instructions: the title of the guide, a paragraph that says to read the guide with `tool_guide` before the first step, and the rules section with MCP tool names; it reads nothing from the folder, so it is the same with or without a workspace, and is at most 4,000 characters long. `instructions` and `skill` cannot be given together.
whileReadOnlyReason: Writes only the skill file, which holds no name of the metamodel, so a missing or faulty metamodel does not stop it.

names.description: How the guide names a command: `cli` as a call of the command line (`reqseq element create`), `mcp` as the name of the MCP tool (`element_create`). The calls for a pipeline stay command-line calls. Ignored with `skill`, which names every command both ways, and with `instructions`, which names every command as MCP tool.

skill.description: Give the skill file instead of the agent guide. It reads nothing from the workspace, so it works without one.

instructions.description: Give the MCP server instructions instead of the agent guide: only the rules, and the call that reads the guide. It reads nothing from the workspace, so it works without one. Not together with `skill`.

write.description: Also write the skill file at each of its places in the repository (needs `skill`): created, replaced when ReqSeq wrote it and nobody changed it, or left when it is the same.

replace.description: Replace a skill file that ReqSeq did not write or that was changed since, at every place (needs `write`).

guide.title: Agent guide
guide.description: The agent guide, with `skill` the skill file, or with `instructions` the MCP server instructions, as Markdown, LF line endings and a final newline.

places.title: Skill file places
places.description: Each place `write` wrote the skill file at, in the order `.claude/…`, then `.agents/…`; only with `write`.

path.description: The skill file at this place, relative to the workspace root, with `/`.

action.title: Done
action.description: `created`: there was no file; `replaced`: the file was replaced; `unchanged`: it was already the file of this version.

previousVersion.title: Previous version
previousVersion.description: The ReqSeq version that wrote the replaced file.
